Bayesian Spike-and-Slab Joint Graphical Lasso

Source: R/ssjgl.R
ssjgl.Rd

Estimates multiple related precision matrices (inverse covariance matrices) across K groups using an EM algorithm with spike-and-slab priors. The method encourages shared sparsity across groups via either fused or group penalties, while allowing group-specific differences through adaptive, edge-specific penalization.

Usage

ssjgl(
  Y,
  penalty = "fused",
  lambda0,
  lambda1,
  lambda2,
  v1 = 1,
  v0s = NULL,
  doubly = FALSE,
  rho = 1,
  a = 1,
  b = 1,
  maxitr.em = 500,
  tol.em = 1e-04,
  maxitr.jgl = 500,
  tol.jgl = 1e-05,
  truncate = 1e-05,
  normalize = FALSE,
  c = 0.1,
  impute = TRUE,
  standardize = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

Y

List of K data matrices, each n_k x p. Missing values (NA) are supported when impute = TRUE.

penalty

Character: "fused" (penalizes pairwise differences between groups) or "group" (penalizes L2 norm across groups).

lambda0

Scalar penalty on diagonal entries of precision matrices. The method is relatively insensitive to this value; lambda0 = 1 is recommended in most cases.

lambda1

Scalar (or matrix) base penalty on off-diagonal entries (edge-wise sparsity). In the prior, each off-diagonal precision entry has a Laplace prior with rate lambda1/v0 in the spike and lambda1/v1 in the slab, so sparsity is governed by the ratio lambda1/v0 (see v0s). Li et al. (2019) use lambda1 = 1 with variables on unit scale, and that is the recommended starting point with standardize = TRUE. If the data are not standardised, the meaning of lambda1 depends on the variables' scales, because the penalty acts on precision entries.

lambda2

Scalar (or matrix) base penalty for the cross-group similarity term. Controls borrowing of strength across groups:

  • lambda2 = 0: no cross-group borrowing (separate estimation)

  • lambda2 = lambda1: equal weight on sparsity and similarity

  • lambda2 > lambda1: encourage more similar graphs across groups

  • lambda2 < lambda1: allow groups to differ more

v1

Numeric slab variance parameter. Default 1. Should generally be left at 1.

v0s

Numeric vector of spike variances, decreasing: the ladder for the dynamic posterior exploration of Li et al. (2019), each step warm-started from the previous one. The spike is a Laplace prior on the precision entries with rate lambda1/v0, i.e. scale v0/lambda1; it is not a normal prior, and sqrt(v0) has no partial-correlation interpretation. Only lambda1/v0 matters. As a rough guide, a non-edge's precision entry is soft-thresholded in the M-step at about lambda1/(n v0) on the covariance scale (the correlation scale for standardised data), for group sample size n. Default NULL uses make_v0_ladder(lambda1), the 3-step ladder lambda1/v0 = 10, 31.6, 100, i.e. v0s = c(0.1, 0.0316, 0.01) at lambda1 = 1. This default was chosen by a simulation study; see vignette("parameter-exploration") and make_v0_ladder. It requires a positive scalar lambda1; otherwise supply v0s.

doubly

Logical. If TRUE, uses doubly spike-and-slab prior with separate indicators for edge existence (delta) and cross-group similarity (xi). Default FALSE.

rho

Numeric ADMM step-size parameter. Default 1.

a

Numeric Beta prior shape1 for inclusion probabilities. Default 1.

b

Numeric Beta prior shape2. Default 1. Setting b = p gives a sparse prior.

maxitr.em

Integer max EM iterations per v0 step. Default 500.

tol.em

Numeric EM convergence tolerance. Default 1e-4.

maxitr.jgl

Integer max ADMM iterations for M-step. Default 500.

tol.jgl

Numeric ADMM convergence tolerance. Default 1e-5.

truncate

Numeric threshold below which entries are zeroed. Default 1e-5.

normalize

Logical. If TRUE, mean-centres each variable within each group. It does not scale. Default FALSE. Centring does not change the estimates, because the sample covariance is centred anyway. When missing values are imputed the data are always centred internally (the conditional-mean imputation assumes mean zero), and the imputed values are returned on the original scale. Kept for back-compatibility; see standardize.

c

Numeric diagonal regularization for initial precision estimate. Default 0.1.

impute

Logical. If TRUE, imputes NAs via conditional MVN at each EM iteration. The M-step then uses the expected sample covariance given the observed data, i.e. the covariance of the imputed data plus the conditional covariance of the missing cells (Li et al., 2019, supplement B). Default TRUE.

standardize

Logical. If TRUE, centres and scales each variable to unit variance within each group before fitting, so the precision matrices are estimated on the correlation scale and lambda1, lambda2 and v0s have the same meaning whatever the variables' units. Recommended unless the variables are already on a common, meaningful scale. Default FALSE (for back-compatibility). Imputed values are returned on the original scale.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, report progress (each EM iteration on the R path, and each ladder step) with message(). Default FALSE.

Value

An object of class "ssjgl". With standardize = TRUE the precision matrices are those of the standardised variables. It is a list with elements:

thetalist

List (length = length(v0s)) of lists of K precision matrices (p x p) at each v0 step.

pi1list

List of pi_delta values (edge inclusion probability) at each v0 step.

pi2list

List of pi_xi values (non-similarity probability) at each v0 step.

fitlist

List of raw JGL fit objects at each v0 step.

itrlist

Integer vector of EM iterations at each v0 step.

problist1

List of p x p edge inclusion probability matrices P(delta=1) at each v0 step.

penlist1

List of p x p adaptive penalty weight matrices for lambda1 at each v0 step.

problist2

List of p x p non-similarity probability matrices P(xi=1). NULL if doubly = FALSE.

penlist2

List of p x p adaptive penalty weights for lambda2. NULL if doubly = FALSE.

timelist

Numeric vector of wall-clock seconds per v0 step.

imputed

Numeric vector of imputed values on the original data scale (one per row of missed), or NULL.

missed

Matrix of (group, row, col) for missing values, or NULL.

v0s, v1, lambda0, lambda1, lambda2, penalty, doubly, a, b

The hyperparameters used.

n, p, K

Sample sizes (length K), number of variables and number of groups.

varnames, groupnames

Variable names (from colnames(Y[[1]]), or V1, ..., Vp) used as dimnames of every p x p output, and group names (from names(Y), possibly NULL).

normalize, standardize, center, scale

The preprocessing used: center is the K x p matrix of column means subtracted (NULL if the data were not centred) and scale the K x p matrix of standard deviations divided by (NULL unless standardize = TRUE).

args

Named list of every argument except Y, as used (with the default v0s filled in); used to refit with the same settings, e.g. by diff_edges.

call

The matched call.

Details

The algorithm follows the dynamic posterior exploration strategy of Li et al. (2019), iterating over a decreasing ladder of spike variances v0s (increasing spike penalty lambda1/v0) with warm-starting between steps.

References

Li, Z. R., McCormick, T. H., & Clark, S. J. (2019). Bayesian Joint Spike-and-Slab Graphical Lasso. ICML 2019.

See also

make_v0_ladder(), plot_path(), plot_stability(), SSJGL_select_v0_cv(), compute_metrics()

Examples

sim <- simulate_ssjgl_data(K = 2, p = 10, n = 50, seed = 1)
fit <- ssjgl(sim$data_list, penalty = "fused",
             lambda0 = 1, lambda1 = 1, lambda2 = 1,
             standardize = TRUE, maxitr.em = 50, impute = FALSE)
fit$v0s  # the default ladder, make_v0_ladder(lambda1 = 1)
#> [1] 0.10000000 0.03162278 0.01000000
print(fit)
#> Spike-and-Slab Joint Graphical Lasso (SSJGL)
#>   Groups (K): 2
#>   Variables (p): 10
#>   v0 ladder steps: 3
#>   Total EM iterations: 24
#>   Total time: 0.2 seconds
#>   Group 1: 10 non-zero edges (from precision)
#>   Group 2: 10 non-zero edges (from precision)
#>   Edges with P(inclusion) > 0.5: 10
adj <- extract_adjacency(fit, threshold = 0.5)
sum(adj[[1]][upper.tri(adj[[1]])])  # estimated edge count
#> [1] 10
